resources.string: When you ask, Ketchup reads the Instagram or Snapchat chat you have open and sends it to Muse Spark for a catch-up. It reads only that chat, only when you tap, and nothing is kept on Ketchup\'s server. It works only in the Instagram and Snapchat apps.
Read the newest messages in this chat and catch up with Muse Spark.
Only this chat, only now. Nothing is kept.
Putting the chat back where it was
Ketchup sends the chat to Muse Spark as you, so it needs your account. Nothing has been read.
Open Ketchup and read what the bubble does before it reads anything. Nothing has been read.
Nothing from the chat was kept.
Open a chat first, then tap the bubble.
Couldn\'t find any messages here. Scroll to the newest message and try again.
The chat changed while Ketchup was reading it. Scroll to the newest message and try again.
Open a chat in %1$s and a small Ketchup bubble floats over it. Tap it, pick the last 30, 80 or 120 messages, and Muse Spark catches you up.
It shows when a chat is open in Instagram or Snapchat.
Turn it on in Android\'s accessibility settings.
%1$s isn\'t on this phone. Install it, sign in, then come back.
Not tested on a real phone yet. Snapchat may not share chat text with other apps at all, so the bubble may find nothing there.

On Android 13 and later, Settings may grey out the switch for apps that didn\'t come from a store. Open Ketchup\'s App info, tap the ⋮ menu, choose Allow restricted settings, then turn the bubble on again.
Not in a released app: Meta\'s and Snap\'s terms don\'t allow reading chats this way.
The Instagram or Snapchat chat you have open, as the app shows it on screen: who said what, and when. Your friends\' messages too.
Only when you tap the bubble and pick how many messages. It scrolls back through that chat, then puts it back. Until you tap, it only checks whether a chat is open, never what it says.
To Muse Spark, through Ketchup\'s server, for your catch-up. The messages aren\'t stored, not on Ketchup\'s server and not on this phone.
Ketchup uses Android\'s accessibility access to read the screen. It only listens to Instagram and Snapchat, and you can turn it off any time in Settings.
In Settings, open Accessibility, then Ketchup catch-up, and turn it on.
